What I want to outline here is a fundamentally different approach to moderation. For lack of a catchier name, I'm calling it the "opt-in overlay" model. I would like to draw attention to it, and start a discussion about its merits and possible improvements.

Monolithic moderation is flawed.

When I say monolithic moderation I am refering to the moderation model we use today. We have an appointed group of humans performing a service for a community. Moderators perform this service by currating the content. Bad content is removed, leaving only good content for consumption.

Issues arise when members of a community feel that good content is mistaken for bad, and subsequently removed. They feel missrepresented. Sometimes this creates schisms in the community. It could be argued that voat was created out of a schism in the reddit community.

The problem is that people are different. They subscribe to different beliefs, have variable amounts of sensitivity, and consider certain things taboo. It is a mistake to believe that it is possible to have a singular, monolithic, classificaton of "Good content" even when applied to a single topic.

What is "opt-in overlay" moderation?

It is moderation that you tailor for yourself. You have the option of subscribing to one or more moderation overlays. Overlay moderators do what moderators have always done, but specific to their topic.

I'll start with an example. Lets say you are a very sensitive individual, and consider topics about "Widget X" distasteful to an extreme. To add a bit of complexity, you also don't care for dressing dogs up in silly outfits. You would subscribe to the "No Widget X" and "No Dog dressing" overlays. After doing so, you would benefit from the work of moderators and come accross much less "Bad content". If you disagreed with how a moderation lense is classifying content, you could switch to another one or start your own. If your moderation overlay is great except for a few bad apples, you could disable the individual moderator's contributions to your lense.

Overlays stack. Overlays are optional. Overlays can come in "budles" to address more general needs. Bans are overlay specific.

I think there is real potential here, a chance to improve moderation for everyone. What do you guys think?
